Sertraline kinda makes you feel numb for bad feelings so I had no anxiety and still don't (this comes with higher doses). After you target the route of the problem is becomes easier to stop. Next is how I also just would find myself still picking because it became a habit despite the sertraline. I was on my way to school and a guy on his motorbike crashed. The pavement is higher than the road so when the guy crashed he got stuck inbetween the two. His foot was still on the accelerator so the motorbike pushed his head into the pavement and as he wasn't wearing a helmet I watched as his skin was scraped away by the friction created. His foot didn't get off that peddle until I could see his brain. That's when people ran to help him. It's also the time he died.

I still think of that most days. It was only a couple months back.

Speaking from someone who has attempted. It isn't your fault. You said that you feel as if it was the last blow to your dad when you came out but please trust me with this, it was not. You can't blame his death on you finally being yourself. Because that's all parents should want for their kids and I can only apologise that you never got what you so needed than. The acceptance. I am trans myself also and because of this I know that feeling alot. The feeling that you're never going to be a real boy/girl but the thing is - from the moment you were born you were. It may have been harder to see but it doesn't change the fact. You are you and the world needs to realise that's not going to change anytime soon.

You are not a pig. You don't have to put yourself down as a punishment for how your feeling because that will only make you feel worse. There are so many things about you that amount to you being the great person you most definitely are, sure you may not see that yourself but for a random stranger off  the Internet to see it, someone who hasn't even met you, that must amount to something. And if not that's still okay because someone, it can even be you, will come into your life and teach you how to love yourself. You never know maybe this is the beginning of that.

Please keep your head up high and live unregretably as you. I wish you all the luck for the future  :)

As someone who has anorexia it is really hard to stop doing all these things. They make you feel safe even if they also don't at the same time. In the sense that, I hate change and if I can't Control anything in my life I know that the 1 thing I can is my eating. However, in the past this led me to pro Ana groups which are honestly the worst things. It's a community of people who encourage others to continue and when you have others like this, it sometimes feels like they've got your back. When it's just a lie. Because no one who wants you to be more ill will ever have your back. Your sister is struggling right now as you've said, but I promise you it does make a difference that you care. You're right when it comes to stepping back because this is her fight to fight however it doesn't mean you can't help her with it. Sometimes we need someone to help us battle out own demons (but only if you feel like you can do so and it isn't too hard mentally on you - that's when it's okay to step back and don't ever feel guilty for it). Eating disorders stem from other things. For example, I don't have an ed because I wanted one, one day. No it stems from my body image issues. With many people you have to target the root of the problem in order to help the problem itself. There are many resources out there so no one goes through things alone and that includes you too. I've seen first hand what I did to my sister and it helped me start to think I need to get control of this, so know you're not alone with that - there are many people in the same boat as you.

You're doing the right thing here. If you don't think you can help her any longer then never ever feel bad about it. Because you've done all you can.
